'''Hot and sour soup''' is a variant of {{xlit|zh|[[hulatang]]}} or "pepper hot soup" ({{langx|zh|胡辣汤}}) that originated from [[Henan cuisine]].<ref>{{Cite book |last=尹同亮 |script-title=zh:字圣故里：漯河 |date=1 January 2011 |publisher=Beijing Book Co. Inc. |isbn=978-7-5349-4802-2 |language=zh |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=qR370AEACAAJ}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book |last=菜馍双全 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=SE68DwAAQBAJ&dq=%E9%85%B8%E8%BE%A3%E6%B1%A4&pg=PT107 |script-title=zh:馋是一枝花：优质吃货的修行札记 |date=1 October 2017 |publisher=Beijing Book Co. Inc. |isbn=978-7-5063-9674-5 |language=zh}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book |last=Lin |first=Grace |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=yNz10AEACAAJ |title=Chinese Menu: The History, Myths, and Legends Behind Your Favorite Foods |date=12 September 2023 |publisher=Little, Brown Books for Young Readers |isbn=978-0-316-48639-2 |language=en}}</ref> Also popular in [[Southeast Asia]], [[India]], [[Pakistan]], and the [[United States]], it is a flexible soup which allows ingredients to be substituted or added depending on availability. For example, the American-Chinese version can be  thicker as it commonly includes corn starch, while in [[Japan]], [[sake]] is often added.
